 ORDER

The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.911/2024 on the files of the Fast Track Special Court,
Chalakkudy, which arose out of Crime No.519/2024 of Chalakkudy Police Station, Thrissur.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections 376, 354 & 354A(1)(i) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (in short, 'IPC') and Section 4(1) read with Section 3(b), Section 8 read with Section 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (in short, 'POCSO Act').
2.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The prosecution case relates to the rape and penetrative sexual assault perpetrated by the petitioner upon the survivor, a minor girl, at the residence of the petitioner at Coimbatore.

The allegation is that, as enticed by the petitioner, the survivor (CW2) left the residence where she had been residing along with her uncle, at Elinjipra, at about 1:00 p.m., on 27.04.2024, and reached the house where the accused has been residing, by night.
It is thereafter that the petitioner/accused is alleged to have resorted to sexual assaults, including penetrative sexual assault, upon that minor girl.

The Trial Court proceeded with the examination of PW1 & PW2 in connection with the charges framed under Sections 376, 354 & 354A(1)(i) of the IPC and Section 3(b) read with 2025:KER:72754 Section 4(1) and Section 7 read with Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

It was at that time, the challenge regarding the territorial jurisdiction of the learned Special Judge, Fast Track Special Court,
Chalakkudy, to proceed with the trial, was raised.

A petition was filed under Section 177 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short, 'Cr.PC'), challenging the authority of the Special Court at Chalakkudy, to proceed with the trial in this case.

As per the order dated 18.12.2024, the learned Special Judge found that the charge in that case ought to be altered, invoking the powers under Section 216 of the Cr.PC, for incorporating the offence under Section 366 IPC.
Accordingly, it was observed in the aforesaid order that a chance will be given to both sides on the question of framing/altering the charge.
It was also observed that the question of recalling witnesses would be considered after the alteration of charges.

3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that the Special Court went wrong in arriving at the aforesaid finding, and that the offences alleged against the petitioner are not triable before the Special Court at Chalakkudy.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

It is apparent from the prosecution records that the allegation levelled against the petitioner pertains to the alleged act of enticing a minor girl and causing her to to be taken to the residence of the petitioner, from the lawful custody of her uncle, who was taking care of her at the place called Elinjipra in Thrissur District, and thereafter resorting to sexual assault, including penetrative sexual assault, upon the survivor at residence of the accused at Coimbatore.
It is true that the alleged acts of sexual assault are said to have been committed at the residence of the petitioner at Coimbatore.

But at the same time, the origin of the crime is from the act of the petitioner enticing the survivor girl through telephone calls and creating a situation wherein the survivor girl was lured to leave the residence of her uncle, to reach the residence of the accused at Coimbatore.

6. Having regard to the above facts and circumstances of the case, the learned Special Judge cannot be found to be at fault for his findings in the order passed on 18.12.2024, in C.M.P.No.423/2024 that the charge against the accused required to be altered for incorporating the offence under Section 366 IPC.

It is well settled that the alteration of charge could be done at any time before the pronouncement of the judgment by the Trial Court, but of course, the Trial Court has to ensure 2025:KER:72754 that the altered charge is read over to the accused, and the witnesses are recalled and further examined for providing an opportunity to the accused to raise his defense against the new accusation.

In the case on hand, the learned Special Judge had observed in the impugned order that a chance will be given to both sides on the question of framing/altering charge,
and that the recall of witnesses will also be considered after the alteration of charge.

In such a situation, it is not possible for this Court to invoke the powers under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to interfere with the proceedings before the Special Court.
There is absolutely no merit in the present petition filed by the petitioner challenging the proceedings of the Trial Court seeking the quashment of the FIR, final report and other records.
The petition is accordingly dismissed.

(Sd/-)
 G. GIRISH, JUDGE DST/29.09.25 Shafeek vs State Of Kerala on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195915480/
